newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T sells two US insurers for $330 mln.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T sells two US insurers for $330 mln.

text.p: B.A.T Industries Plc, the tobacco to financial services group, said on Friday its U.S. insurance arm Farmers Group Inc had agreed the sale of two units to a branch of Americo Life Inc for a total of about $330 million.

In a statement, B.A.T said that Farmers sale of the units -- Columbus-based Ohio State Life Insurance and Investors Guaranty Life Insurance, -- was in line with its strategic plan to focus on growth in its Farmers New World Life Insurance Company, which markets its products and services directly rather than through independent organisations as these firms do.
"The disposal will result in no material impact on Farmers' trading profit," the British company said in a statement.
At the end of 1995 the two companies being sold had a combined 231,000 life insurance policies in force.
Farmers, based in Los Angeles, manages the third-largest auto and home insurers in the United States as well as a major commercial lines insurer.
B.A.T shares were little changed after the deal's announcement and at 1420 GMT were down 3-1/2 pence at 498 pence, roughly in line with the overall market trend.
